response: {"title":"Existing-checks-first budget","intervention":"Spend the first 80% of verification time on existing checks selected by changed-module and caller relevance, ordered shortest first, and use at most the final 20% to create a new focused check only for the highest-risk behavior not covered by those checks.","claim":"Relative to no appended instruction, this existing-checks-first budget will increase hidden-test pass_rate without increasing deadline misses on multi-module Python tasks.","mechanism":"Reusing existing checks avoids test-construction overhead and shortest-first ordering rapidly accumulates evidence, while a small protected allocation fills the single most consequential coverage gap.","assumptions":["Relevant existing checks are discoverable from module and caller names.","Existing tests have lower setup cost than new focused checks.","A rough runtime ordering can be inferred or measured."],"risks":["Existing checks may encode obsolete behavior or weak assertions.","Shortest-first can prioritize many low-value microtests.","The 20% allocation may be insufficient to create and run the missing check.","Caller relevance may omit event-driven or configuration-mediated consumers."],"test_plan":{"experiment":"Randomly assign matched fixed-deadline multi-module Python tasks to this appended instruction or no appended instruction, holding model, tools, and hidden-test scoring constant.","metrics":["pass_rate","wall_time","turns"],"success_condition":"Treatment produces higher pass_rate with no increase in deadline-miss rate; wall_time and turns indicate whether test-reuse saves effort."},"single_shot_ordinal":12}
